name: Sekai Ichi

origin.place: Aomori Apple Experiment Station, Aomori, Japan

history: From a 1930 cross of Delicious and Golden Delicious at the Aomori Apple Experiment Station; the seedling first fruited in 1946 and was registered (as Aori 4) in 1974. The popular name, meaning 'world's number one', began as a trial grower's boast about its size, and it is sold mainly as a luxury gift apple in Japan and East Asia.

look.description: Huge round to conical apple, typically 500-800 g and sometimes over 1 kg, yellow-green almost covered in bright red stripes.

taste.summary: Mild and gently sweet with very little acidity and little aroma; the dense flesh is crunchy and very juicy. Prized for size and looks more than intensity.

tree.notes: Top-grade fruit depends on careful thinning and good light; the very largest fruits keep less well.

pollination.notes: Diploid and self-incompatible (S3S9); UK flowering group not recorded.

climate.best_climates: Cool northern Japan (Aomori), with a warm summer and a cool, sunny autumn.
climate.poor_climates: Little grown outside Japan; no reliable data from hot or very short-season climates.

grow_notes: A curiosity for growers who want giant fruit: thin hard to one fruit per cluster and give the tree full sun. Pick in October and keep cold; plant a mid-season diploid partner.

name: Hokuto

origin.place: Aomori Apple Experiment Station, Aomori, Japan
origin.parentage: Registered as Fuji x Mutsu, but later genetic work indicates the pollen parent was not Mutsu and is unidentified

history: Selected from a 1970 cross at the Aomori Apple Experiment Station, named in 1981 and registered in 1983. It was released as Fuji x Mutsu, but DNA studies since then point to a different pollen parent. Japanese tasters rate it among the best-flavoured apples, though it remains a niche variety.

look.description: Large, round to flattish apple, usually about 350 g and often over 600 g, deep purplish-red with stripes over a yellow ground.

taste.summary: Exceptionally juicy, firm cream flesh with a balanced sweet-sharp taste and a rich scent; fully ripe fruit often has watercore, giving glassy, honey-sweet patches.

tree.notes: Needs plenty of sun to colour. Listed as triploid by Pomiferous; given the doubt over its pollen parent, treat this as provisional.

pollination.notes: If triploid, a poor pollen donor: plant with two compatible diploids. UK flowering group not recorded.

climate.poor_climates: Little grown outside Japan; dull or short seasons are likely to leave this late apple under-coloured.

health.other: Prone to watercore and to mouldy core, which spoils the centre but not the surrounding flesh.

grow_notes: Plant in the sunniest spot available with two diploid pollinators. Pick in late October or early November, store cold and eat by late winter, cutting out any mouldy core.
